title: Robust structured-output fuzzing + backcompat checks for JSON mode
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an automated test harness and fuzzing pipeline that validates JSON-mode enforcement, constrained-decoding behavior, and schema adherence across server runtime and all SDKs (Python, JS, Go). This ticket covers mutation/fuzz tests, golden-schema snapshots, cross-version compatibility checks, and telemetry for parser failures.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzzing harness can mutate prompts and model outputs and detect violations of required schema fields with reproducible minimization
End-to-end tests run in CI for runtime-1.20 and latest hosted runtime verifying JSON mode flag produces strict JSON responses for supported models
SDKs (python/js/go) include test adapters that validate SDK-level constrained-decoding fallback paths and raise clear errors when decoding is ambiguous
Console shows aggregated parser error rates and schema-drift alerts in the structured-output dashboard during the PR validation window
Backcompat checks run weekly comparing new runtime builds to a golden snapshot; any new schema relaxations must be explicitly approved in PR description
tasks: Design mutation strategy: templates, token-level corruptions, whitespace/escape variants
Implement harness that runs mutated prompts through hosted endpoint, dedicated runtime, and private devbox
Add minimizer to reduce failing examples to smallest reproducible prompt/response pair
Integrate with OSS fuzzing library (afl-like) for token-stream mutations
Add adapters in python/js/go SDK test suites to parse and assert constrained-decoding behavior
Pipeline to snapshot golden schemas and diff tooling to surface unintended changes
Wire parser failure telemetry to Console and create a schema-drift alert rule
Document failure triage playbook and remediation steps for runtime, model, and SDK authors
progress_updates: 2025-02-17: Spike completed comparing existing JSON-mode tests across SDKs. Observed JS SDK had looser fallback that accepted trailing comma variants.
2025-02-20: PoC harness committed: rust-based minimizer + python runner. PoC reproduces a case where KV-cache truncation caused partial JSON tokens.
2025-02-24: Design review with Runtime team. Decided runtime will annotate responses with 'x-json-validated' header on strict enforcement path to speed detection in tests.
2025-02-27: Added initial SDK adapters in python and node. Go adapter prototype pending (blocked by serialization util).

2025-03-01: CI job 'structured-output-fuzz' added to infra alpha group; runs nightly against staging models. First night produced 12 parser errors, 3 reduced to minimal repros and uploaded to artifacts.
risks: False positives from overly aggressive mutation rules increasing flakiness in CI
Model variance in free-form models may produce nondeterministic failures unless we pin seeds or use deterministic sampling
Runtime changes that improve latency may alter tokenization boundaries, causing regressions in constrained decoding
Large corpus of failing minimizations could overwhelm triage without explicit ownership and throttling
notes: Keep mutation rules conservative at first: avoid random byte flips inside quoted numeric literals to reduce unhelpful noise
We will use the 'x-json-validated' header as a fast path in tests; the runtime retains a secondary token-level validator for deeper checks
Coordinate with Eval team to reuse existing prompt/response corpora as seed inputs
Consider later adding a model-compatibility matrix in Console indicating which model families support strict JSON mode reliably
qa_plan: Run fuzzing harness in ephemeral staging and collect artifacts for all failures
Triage by assigning to runtime/sdk owners via a Slack alert channel and GH issue auto-creation
Verify minimizer outputs reproduce locally and add regression tests to the relevant repo
Postmortem template for recurring failures with classification: runtime-bug / model-variance / sdk-parsing / prompt-ambiguity
review_feedback: PM review (Rajat): add explicit rollback criteria if parser-error rate > 0.5% in production
Design review (Anya): include examples of allowed 'structured slack' where minor non-critical schema fields can be relaxed
Security review (Lena): ensure fuzzing infrastructure does not run arbitrary customer prompts; only use sanitized corpus
